#41 [ada/finding] G1-ext and Theorem W (PROVED; ada/notes.md R5.1, R5.3), by a Fubini-Study distance argument. G1-ext: start |d>|a0>; free ops are any x-diagonal unitaries with ancillas; units are 1-(1-e^{ib})|d><d|(x)E. After k units ||Pi_G phi|| <= sin((2k+1)theta) for (2k+1)theta <= pi/2. The free ops preserve the bad subspace B, a unit moves every ray of B by <= 2theta, and dist(U psi,B) <= dist(psi,B)+2theta. With adaptive restarts E[D-calls] >= C_AD(p), so phase-adjusted AA is EXACTLY optimal in the G1 class (this replaces R4.1 Claim 3). THEOREM W: the free ops are threshold-type, Pi_G(x)V_G + (1-Pi_G)(x)V_B (arbitrary on the good sector, ancilla-only on the bad sector). The units are D-reflections or walls 1-(1-e^{ia})P(x)E, where P is ANY projector with Pd = d; they may come in any order, with any number of targets. Then success after K units is <= sin^2((2K+1)theta), and E[D-calls per success] >= C_AD(p), attained without walls. Proof: take the reference subspace S = b0(x)A, where b0 is the bad part of d. S lies in B, the free ops preserve S, and dist(d,S) = theta. For walls, w = <b0|P|b0> = (1-2p+||P Pi_G d||^2)/(1-p) >= 1-p, because ||P Pi_G d|| >= |<d|Pi_G d>| = p (Cauchy-Schwarz, d in ran P). So |1-(1-e^{ia})w| >= 2w-1 >= cos 2theta: a wall moves b0 by <= 2theta, exactly like D. This CLOSES W1 for threshold-type phases, including all run39/40 mixed patterns, for any number of targets, with no Jordan diagonalisation of three projectors. Unique-target reduction (PROVED, R5.2): V = span{d, P_x g, g} is invariant, dim <= 3, and depends only on (p, p_max). Numerical agreement: logs/run41 (66 (p,p_max) points, all 254 patterns K <= 7) has max excess 3.1e-15. logs/run42 (300 random generic models with Haar good-sector unitaries, plus optimised K <= 4) has max excess 2.2e-16, with dist(psi,b0) <= (2K+1)theta throughout. Prior work: the rotation-angle method is standard (Hoyer quant-ph/0006031 Thms 2-3). }# ada round 1: adiabatic state preparation (Q = P08) x optimisation-to-decoding reduction (P = P19)

Setting throughout: DQI for max-XORSAT (q = 2), as in 2408.08292 sec. "DQI for max-XORSAT".
B in F_2^{m x n} (rank n), v in F_2^m, f(x) = sum_i (-1)^{v_i + b_i.x} (= #sat - #unsat),
F = sum_i (-1)^{v_i} Z^{b_i} (diagonal, <x|F|x> = f(x)), C_perp = ker B^T, distance d_perp.
The DQI error register holds y (|y| <= l) and the syndrome register holds s = B^T y.
p(y) = w_k^2 / C(m,k) for |y| = k is the DQI error distribution, where w is the principal
eigenvector of the tridiagonal A^{(m,l,0)} with off-diagonals a_k = sqrt(k(m-k+1)) (2408.08292,
Lemma genw / eq. A_def, r/p = 1/2).

## A. Adiabatic coherent decoder (P08 implements the decoder oracle of P19)

### A1. Decoding Hamiltonian (syndrome-controlled)
On an m-qubit work register y' and the n-qubit syndrome register s:

    H_dec = sum_i (1 - Z_i)/2  +  lam * sum_{j=1}^n (1 - Z_{s_j} prod_{i in N(j)} Z_i)/2,
    N(j) = {i : B_ij = 1}  (constraints containing variable j; |N(j)| = variable degree D_j).

H_dec commutes with every Z_{s_j}; on the s-sector it is H_s(y') = |y'| + lam * #{j : (B^T y')_j != s_j}.
It is a single *uncontrolled* Hamiltonian of 1-local and (D_j + 1)-local Z-strings: the syndrome
bit simply joins the parity check. Driver: -sum_i X_i on the work register only.
Path: H(u) = -(1-u) sum_i X_i + u H_dec, u = u(t/T); initial state |+^m> for every s.

**Lemma A1 (proved).** If d_perp >= 2l+1, |y*| <= l, s = B^T y*, and lam >= l+1, then y* is the
unique ground state of H_s, and the gap of H_s is >= 1.
Proof: H_s is diagonal with integer values. Any y' != y* with B^T y' = s lies in y* + C_perp, so
|y'| >= d_perp - |y*| >= l+1 > |y*|. Any y' with at least one violated check has H_s(y') >= lam >= l+1 > |y*|.

### A2. Compute-copy-uncompute (CCU) and exact error formula
Let U_s be the adiabatic evolution in the s-sector; U_s|+^m> = sum_z u_z(s)|z>, alpha_s = u_{y*(s)}(s).
The decoder V = (U^dag on work)(CNOT work -> error register)(U on work), followed by H^{⊗m} on the work register.

**Lemma A2 (proved).** For the DQI input sum_y a_y |y>_err |B^T y>_syn |+^m>_work (a_y supported on
|y| <= l with 2l < d_perp), the overlap of the output with the ideal state sum_y a_y |0>|B^T y>|+^m> is

    O = sum_y |a_y|^2 |alpha_{B^T y}|^2 = 1 - E_{y~p}[eps_s^2],   eps_s^2 := 1 - |alpha_s|^2.

The overlap is real and non-negative: the syndrome-dependent dynamical and geometric phases of U_s cancel exactly.
Proof: syndromes of distinct y in the ball are distinct (2l < d_perp), so branches are orthogonal. In branch y,
projecting the error register onto |0> after the CNOT selects z = y, giving u_y|y>_work, and
<+|U_s^dag|y> = conj(u_y). Hence the branch overlap is |u_y|^2.
Consequence: trace distance to the ideal DQI state = sqrt(1 - O^2) <= sqrt(2 E_p[eps_s^2]).
This is the card's O(sqrt(p_fail)) with p_fail := E_p[eps_s^2] (adiabatic leakage probability averaged over the
DQI error distribution). If instead the error register is not post-selected, the same bound holds for the
reduced state of the syndrome register.

**Negative result A2' (numerical, with the exact reason).** A single reverse adiabatic run on the error register,
|y*> -> e^{i phi_s}|+^m>, uses one evolution instead of two but leaves the phases e^{i phi_s}, which depend on the syndrome.
The overlap is then |E_p[conj(alpha_s)]|, which does not converge as T grows (logs/run02, run06). So the single run is
not a valid decoder unless phi_s is independent of s, which no symmetry known to me guarantees.

### A3. Cost and assumptions
- Qubits: m (error) + n (syndrome) + m (work) + O(1) parity ancilla. No arithmetic or message registers.
  For comparison, the reversible BP and Berlekamp-Massey decoders in 2408.08292 sec. resources need ~9e3 logical
  qubits at p = 521. 2504.18334 uses reversible Gauss-Jordan elimination, which only covers 2l < d_perp
  with small codes; I have not inspected its resource numbers in detail.
- Time per DQI sample: 2T of evolution under H(u), with ||H'(u)|| <= 2m + lam*n (linear schedule).
  Per Trotter step: m X-rotations, m Z-rotations, and n parity rotations of weight D_j + 1 (2 D_j CNOTs each).
- Additional assumption, which is new compared with P19: a **uniform gap promise**. Because s is in superposition the
  schedule must be fixed in advance, so T is set by Delta_min = min over s in the support (|y| <= l) of min_u Delta_s(u).
  With the Jansen-Ruskai-Seiler bound (quant-ph/0603175, as quoted in the P08 contract) and a linear schedule,
  eps_s <= C[ (||H'(0)||/Delta_s(0)^2 + ||H'(1)||/Delta_s(1)^2 + 7 ∫ ||H'||^2/Delta_s^3 ) ] / T, so
  T = O((m + lam n)^2 / (Delta_min^3 eps)) suffices for eps_s <= eps for all s. Boundary-cancelling schedules or eigenpath
  traversal (P08 variants) improve the eps and Delta dependence asymptotically. For the randomised eigenpath variant the
  same classical random times must be reused in compute and uncompute.
- Error behaviour: the overlap loss is quadratic in the leakage amplitude (Lemma A2). The trace-distance contribution is
  sqrt(2) * rms(eps_s), linear in the rms leakage amplitude. Trotter error adds linearly (checked: dt = 0.02 vs 0.01 agree
  to 2e-5 in O; run02 vs run05).

### A4. Scope and limitations (assessment)
- A per-branch decoder: it computes y*(s) as a function of s, so it is limited exactly as classical decoders are
  (unique or ML decoding: the Shannon-type limit in 2408.08292 sec. limits). It does **not** exploit the coherence of the
  errors (the Holevo regime discussed there), because the s register already carries the full information that reaches the decoder.
- Its runtime is set by the gap of a transverse-field Ising decoding Hamiltonian with (D+1)-body parity terms. For
  growing m at fixed l/m this is a planted-solution problem. Transverse-field annealing on planted 3-regular 3-XORSAT is known
  to have exponentially small gaps (Farhi et al. 1208.3757 and Jörg et al.; neither inspected in this round, cited from memory,
  so treat as unverified). The field term sum_i n_i here favours the all-zero string, which may change this picture at small l/m.
  Conjecture A4 (open): for codes C_perp whose parity-check graph is a good vertex expander, Delta_min = Omega(1) up to a constant
  error fraction l/m, mirroring Sipser-Spielman flip decoding. No evidence beyond m <= 12.
- Where it could matter: codes with no efficient *reversible* classical decoder, or where qubit count rather than gate count is the
  binding constraint. It is not expected to beat reversible BP on sparse LDPC instances in gate count.

## B. Structural result: the DQI state as a restricted ground state (S1)
F~ := H^{⊗n} F H^{⊗n} = sum_i (-1)^{v_i} X^{b_i} acts on the syndrome register as a signed Cayley-graph adjacency of F_2^n
with generators b_i. Ball_l := span{|B^T y> : |y| <= l}, with projector Pi_l.

**Proposition S1 (proved).** If 2l+1 < d_perp then:
(a) |y> -> (-1)^{v.y}|B^T y> is an isometry from the radius-l Hamming ball of F_2^m onto Ball_l;
(b) under it, Pi_l F~ Pi_l equals the adjacency matrix of the m-cube restricted to the radius-l ball (all signs gauge away,
because the ball contains no cycle of the Cayley graph: cycles correspond to codewords of C_perp);
(c) the top eigenvector is unique (Perron-Frobenius on a connected graph) and S_m-invariant, hence equals sum_k w_k |S_k>, the
optimal DQI state, with eigenvalue lambda_max(A^{(m,l,0)}).
Corollary: optimal DQI = ground state of -Pi_l F~ Pi_l; it is optimal among **all** states whose Fourier support lies in
{B^T y : |y| <= l}, i.e. all amplitude functions that are multilinear of degree <= l in the constraint signs, not only
symmetric polynomials of f. (Novelty unclear; 2408.08292 optimises over P(f) only, in sec. semicircle.)
Proof of (b): for |y|,|y'| <= l, <B^T y'|X^{b_i}|B^T y> = 1 iff B^T(y' + y + e_i) = 0; since |y'+y+e_i| <= 2l+1 < d_perp this
forces y' = y + e_i. The sign is (-1)^{v.y'+v_i+v.y} = (-1)^{v.(y'+y+e_i)} = 1.
Checked numerically: logs/run08 (line "S1 check").

## R5.1 Proposition G1-ext (PROVED): exact optimality of phase-adjusted AA among D-reflection circuits with ancillas
Class: start |d>|a0> (1 D-call). Free: any x-diagonal unitary sum_x |x><x| (x) V_x (cost phases, threshold phases,
reversible arithmetic, coherent copies of x = deferred measurement). Units (2 D-calls): 1 - (1 - e^{ib}) |d><d| (x) E,

Proof. Fubini-Study distance on rays; dist(psi, S) = min over rays of S, and ||Pi_G psi|| = sin dist(psi, B).
 (i) Free operations map B onto B (they preserve each x), so they preserve dist(., B).
 (ii) A unit U equals 1 (x) E^perp + D_b (x) E, with D_b = 1 - (1 - e^{ib})|d><d|. Write d = cos theta b0 + sin theta g0.
 D_b acts only on span{b0, g0} and fixes the rest of B. For s in B, the B-component of U s has norm^2 >= 1 - (1 - cos^2 2theta) = cos^2 2theta,
 since |<b0|D_b b0>| = |1 - (1 - e^{ib}) cos^2 theta| >= |cos 2theta|. So every ray of U(B) is within 2 theta of B,
 and the same holds for U^{-1}.
 (iii) dist(U psi, B) = dist(psi, U^{-1} B) <= dist(psi, s*) + dist(s*, U^{-1} B) <= dist(psi, B) + 2 theta, where s* is
 the ray of B closest to psi.
 Starting from dist(d, B) = theta gives the claim. []
Corollary (restarts, adaptive). By the G1 Claim 2 argument with s_i <= B_{K_i}: 1 = sum q_i s_i <= E[cost] max_K B_K/(1+2K).

(Hoyer) AA is therefore EXACTLY optimal in this class. Standard pi-AA(k*) is within the sampled factor 1.0516 of it.

## R5.2 Exact reduction for a unique target (PROVED, elementary)
For G = {x*}, V = span{d, P_x|x*>, |x*>} is invariant under |x*><x*|, P_x and |d><d| (d in ran P_x), so dim V <= 3. In the
basis e1 = u = P_x g/||P_x g||, e2 = part of d orthogonal to u, e3 = (1 - P_x) g/||.||, one has g = (sqrt pm, 0,
sqrt(1-pm)) and d = (cos beta, sin beta, 0) with cos^2 beta = p/pm. The whole threshold-phase/D/W problem depends only
on (p, p_max). Special cases: pm = p gives d = u and W equivalent to D. pm = 1 gives W trivial on V. Walls plus threshold
phases alone reach at most p/pm success, because |<e2|psi>| is changed only by D.
Numerics (ada/w1_reduced.py, logs/run41_w1_reduced.log): 66 grid points p in [0.02, 0.6], p/pm in [0.03, 0.9], all

number of targets is allowed.

Compared with B_1 = sin^2(3 theta), theta = arcsin sqrt(P(G)) (threshold-type bound, Theorem W) on the SAME instance.
The optimal phases phi_x = conj(sign(v_x d_x)) depend on x*: this probes the G1/G2 class, not an implementable policy.

import argparse
import math

import numpy as np

from f1_gm import Inst

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--r", type=int, required=True)
ap.add_argument("--t", type=int, required=True)
ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="+", default=[200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 205])

print(f"K=1 arbitrary x-phase + one wall, exact optimum on one optimum x*; r={a.r} t={a.t}")
for s in a.seeds:
    I = Inst(a.r, a.t, s)
    n = I.n
    G = np.nonzero(I.f >= I.fmax)[0]
    xs = int(G[0])
    S = np.nonzero(I.S.inball)[0].astype(np.uint64)
    X = np.arange(1 << n, dtype=np.uint64)

    pG = float(np.sum(np.abs(I.dx[G]) ** 2))
    th = math.asin(math.sqrt(pG))
    B1 = 1.0 if 3 * th >= math.pi / 2 else math.sin(3 * th) ** 2
    dstar = abs(I.dx[xs])
    rest = float(np.sum(np.abs(v * I.dx)) - abs(v[xs] * I.dx[xs]))
    best = 0.0
    for al in np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 20001):
        e = complex(math.cos(al), math.sin(al))

def B_K(p, K):

    PU = np.stack([Pc[c] / np.linalg.norm(comp[c]) for c in bad], axis=1)

    mu = np.linalg.eigvalsh((M + M.T) / 2)
    worst = float(np.min(np.abs(1 - 2 * mu)))

    fnf = max(float(np.max([np.ptp(Pc[c].real[inv == b]) for b in range(L)])) for c in range(L))
    print(f"   c_c(x) spread over x in G: {spreadG:.3e}; max within-level spread of P Pi_c d (0 iff function of f): {fnf:.3e}")
    # (2) exact K=1 scalar score phases + one wall, per target, verified
    best_tot = 0.0
    for j, xs in enumerate(G[: min(len(G), 3)]):
        cc = cG[j]
        dst = d[xs].real
        cst = cc[top]
        V = cst / dst

        a = math.acos(1 - 2 * tau)

        Y1 = wall(amp1, aa)

        print(f"   target {j}: d*^2={dst**2:.4f} V={V:.4f} R={R:.4f} | scalar K=1: P(x*)={g*g:.4f} (sim {sim:.4f}, P(G) sim {simG:.4f}) "

i.e. whether it becomes a restart-normalised gain. Best-found values only (ada/notes.md R6.4).
Usage: python w1c_allw.py > logs/run56_w1c_allw.log
"""
import math
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import minimize
import walled_dynamics as wd
from f1_gm import Inst
from w1c_multik_lib import B_K, c_ad

I = Inst(5, 2, 204)
n, d = I.n, I.dx.real.astype(complex)
mask = I.S.inball.astype(float)
vals, inv = np.unique(I.f, return_inverse=True)
L, top = len(vals), len(vals) - 1
G = inv == top
p = float(np.sum(np.abs(d[G]) ** 2))
Kst = min(range(1, 60), key=lambda K: (1 + 2 * K) / B_K(p, K))
print(f"(5,2) seed 204 p={p:.5f} C_AD={c_ad(p):.3f} attained at K={Kst} (B_K={B_K(p, Kst):.4f})", flush=True)


def run(z, K):
    X = d.copy()
    for j in range(K):
        X = np.exp(1j * z[j * (L + 1): j * (L + 1) + L][inv]) * X
        X = X - (1 - np.exp(1j * z[j * (L + 1) + L])) * wd.wht(mask * wd.wht(X, n), n)
    return float(np.sum(np.abs(X[G]) ** 2))


rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
prev = None
for K in range(1, 9):
    unit = np.zeros(L + 1); unit[top] = math.pi; unit[L] = math.pi
    starts = [np.tile(unit, K)] + [rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi, K * (L + 1)) for _ in range(2)]
    if prev is not None:
        starts.append(np.concatenate([prev, unit]))
    best, bz = 0.0, None
    for z0 in starts:
        res = minimize(lambda z: -run(z, K), z0, method="L-BFGS-B", options={"maxfun": 20000})
        if -res.fun > best:
            best, bz = -res.fun, res.x
    prev = bz
    print(f"K={K}: all-wall best-found {best:.5f} vs B_K={B_K(p, K):.5f} ratio {best / B_K(p, K):.4f} | "
          f"(1+2K)/best = {(1 + 2 * K) / best:.3f} vs C_AD = {c_ad(p):.3f}", flush=True)

import math


def B_K(p, K):
    th = math.asin(math.sqrt(p))
    return 1.0 if (2 * K + 1) * th >= math.pi / 2 else math.sin((2 * K + 1) * th) ** 2


def c_ad(p):
    return min((1 + 2 * K) / B_K(p, K) for K in range(0, 2000))

- (3) Restart optimality is for FRESH-START attempts: each attempt prepares d anew, applies a unitary circuit whose
  length K is fixed before its terminal measurement, and later attempts may depend on earlier failures. It does NOT cover
  variable stopping with intermediate measurements that keep the failed state. Example (verifier): measure the threshold
  on d; on failure keep b0, apply a pi D-reflection and measure again. D b0 = b0 - 2 cos(theta) d, so the good probability is
  4p(1-p) and the bad remainder is again proportional to b0. E[D-calls] = 1 + 1/(2p) = 8/3 < C_AD(0.3) = 3 (checked by hand).
  Threshold checks are counted separately. This model is excluded from all C_AD-optimality statements.
- (4) Proof wording (R5.1, R5.3): read "moves every ray by <= 2 theta" as follows. For every unit s in S, ||Pi_S U s|| >= c,
  where c = |1 - (1 - e^{ia}) w|. With S = b0 (x) A, Pi_S R_a Pi_S = (1 - (1 - e^{ia}) w) |b0><b0| (x) 1, so
  ||Pi_S U s||^2 = ||(1 (x) E^perp) s||^2 + c^2 ||(1 (x) E) s||^2 >= c^2. Hence dist(Us, S) <= arccos c <= 2 theta. U^{-1} has
  the same form with -a and the same modulus, so dist(U^{-1}s, S) <= 2 theta as well. Then
  dist(U psi, S) = dist(psi, U^{-1} S) <= dist(psi, s*) + dist(s*, U^{-1} S), with dist(s*, U^{-1}S) = dist(U s*, S) (Fubini-Study
  triangle inequality). Useful regime: p <= 1/2, so cos 2theta >= 0. For p > 1/2, K = 0 is already optimal and the bound is
  not needed. Free good-sector operations are a block direct sum: an arbitrary unitary on G (x) A plus 1_B (x) V_B on B (x) A.
  This corrects the tensor expression.
- (5) Attainability of B_K. For K < K* := min{K : (2K+1) theta >= pi/2}, standard pi-AA reaches sin^2((2K+1)theta). At K*,
  Hoyer's arbitrary-phase iterate reaches success 1 (quant-ph/0006031, "Obtaining success probability 1", l.356-407, as
  inspected in R5.0). Each of its K* units is one threshold phase plus one D-reflection with an adjusted phase (2 D-calls).
  No extra initial or final phases are needed. C_AD counts decoder calls only: forward preparations plus adjoints. It
  assumes known p and threshold. Threshold phases, zero-reflections and terminal classical checks are not costed. C_AD
  is not a total-resource optimum or an unknown-p procedure.
- (6) Theorem W proves that walls cannot beat the optimal all-D comparator in its restricted model. It does not explain
  the strict percentage losses observed in run39/40, prove locally found mixed angles optimal, or exclude ties. R5.2's
  3-dim reduction holds only for the three-projector threshold-phase model.
- (7) R5.5 repaired by ada/w1_xphase_fix.py (logs/run54, run55). The K = 1 optimum is closed-form, with no angle grid:
  tau = (1 - cos a)/2, g(tau) = d* sqrt(1 - 4V(1-V) tau) + 2 R sqrt(tau), and g is concave. Here V = P[x*,x*] <= 1/4 and
  R >= d*(1 - V), so tau = 1 (a = pi) is optimal (R6.1). The attaining phases are written out coordinate by coordinate.
  For the target x*, phi_* = -arg((1 + (e^{ia}-1)V) d*) = 0. For x != x*, phi_x = -arg((e^{ia}-1) v_x d_x), i.e. pi if
  v_x d_x > 0, else 0. Simulated values agree with the closed form to 4 digits, e.g. (31,10) s202 0.0954 vs B_1 0.0707 and
  (63,12) s200 0.0535 vs 0.0262. The script maximises P(x*) for one selected optimum. For multiple optima the simulated
  P(G) is also printed, e.g. (31,10) s200 0.1161, still below B_1 = 0.3794. "Full G1/G2 class" in R5.5 now reads
  "wall-augmented G2 class". These violations do not contradict G1-ext.
- (8) Information statements narrowed. The phase-alignment prescription uses a selected solution. No information lower
  bound or necessity theorem is proved. Nothing here implies that every helpful score-phase policy must encode the solution.
- (9)-(10) Accepted as stated. Read 'oracle-tuned capacity' as 'best-found per-instance tuned performance'.
  K_tot = 1 + 2k_D + 2k_W in G2's D-call expression; elsewhere K = number of units. The two-flags-per-stage-1-layer count
  is amortised: it uses the trivial initial wall on d and merged inter-layer phases, and the stage join contributes one
  extra boundary flag. Displayed C/WQ costs do not execute the identity initial wall phase. The preparation of d (1 D-call)
  is added once per attempt. Old logs are kept as historical evidence and were not regenerated.
- (11) Theorem W is a related upper bound under a different model, not a formal converse of oblivious AA (1312.1414
  l.541-555). Marriott-Watrous in-place amplification and Nagaj-Wocjan-Zhang amplification have NOT been inspected in this
  round, so the novelty comparison is incomplete (gap recorded). Construction A still lacks comparison with adiabatic
  syndrome decoding and standard coherent error reduction.

## R6.1 W1c, exact K = 1 for score-function phases (PROVED analytically; evaluated and simulated on 24 instances)
Class: start d. Free: Phi = sum_c Pi_c (x) V_c, any (ancilla-controlled) function of the score level c; f(x) in
{vals}; threshold thr = f_max; G = top level. One unit: wall W(a) = 1 - (1 - e^{ia}) P, P = P_x = H Pi_l H (P d = d), or
controlled 1 (x) E^perp + W (x) E. Instances: dual-BCH (r,t) in {(5,2),(6,2),(5,3),(6,3)}, seeds 200-205, with
2l+1 < d_perp asserted, i.e. (31,10,l=1), (63,12,1), (31,15,2), (63,18,2). Abstract exact decoder.
d is a function of f: d_x = P(f(x)), the DQI polynomial. Hence Pi_c d is proportional to 1_{f=c} and its sign is fixed.
Proposition K1 (PROVED, elementary). Fix one target x*, with d* = d_{x*} > 0 WLOG. Let c_c = (P Pi_c d)(x*) (real), so
sum_c c_c = (P d)(x*) = d*. Let V = c_top/d* = P[x*,x*] for a unique target, R = sum_{c != top} |c_c| and
N = (R - d*(1 - V))/2 >= 0 (the 'negative-level mass': the total |c_c| over bad levels whose c_c has the sign opposite to their sum).
Scalar score phases then give max P(x*) = max_{tau in [0,1]} g(tau)^2, with g(tau) = d* sqrt(1 - 4V(1-V) tau) + 2R sqrt(tau). This
is concave in tau, with stationary point tau0 = R^2/(kR^2 + k^2 d*^2/4), k = 4V(1-V). If V <= 1/4, then tau0 >= 1, because
R(1 - 2V) >= d*(1-V)(1-2V) >= 2V(1-V) d*. So a = pi is optimal and max P(x*) = (sqrt(p_*)(3 - 4V) + 4N)^2, with p_* = d*^2.
For a unique target (p = p_*, sin 3theta = 3 sqrt p - 4 p^{3/2}):
   K = 1 score-phase walls beat the threshold-type bound B_1  <=>  N > sqrt(p) (V - p).
Note V >= p (d in ran P), with N = 0 for threshold phases. The attaining policy at a = pi is: phase pi on every bad level
with c_c > 0 (equivalently, a global sign plus phase pi on the target level and on the levels with c_c < 0), then a
pi-wall. For multiple optima, sum_{x in G} max_phi |A(x)|^2 is a certified upper bound on P(G) for this class. On every
instance the shared phases of the first target attained it exactly (simulated).
RESULTS (logs/run48-run51, each value also checked by direct simulation of the circuit on 2^n amplitudes):
 (31,10) 1/6 instances above B_1: s204 (unique) 0.1002 vs 0.0971. Four below, e.g. s202 0.0698 vs 0.0707 (N = 0.0017 <
   N_crit = 0.0021).
 (63,12) 6/6 above B_1, e.g. s200 (unique) 0.0268 vs 0.0262 and s204 (|G| = 3) 0.0637 vs 0.0627.
 (31,15) 6/6 above, e.g. s200 (|G| = 2) 0.0567 vs 0.0537.
 (63,18) 6/6 above, e.g. s200 (unique) 0.0055 vs 0.0051 (+8%) and s204 0.0045 vs 0.0042.
 So 19 of 24 instances violate the per-K form of W1 for score phases at K = 1. The excess is 1-8% in probability.
 The ancilla-controlled class (target branch partly bypassing the wall) gave the same optimum, with s = 1, on all 24
 (numerical: tau grid of 2e4 points, exact inner maximisation; not proved).
 Sign patterns of c_c (bad levels, low -> high): one to three NEGATIVE levels in the middle of the score range. Examples:
 (63,18): ++++++-++--+++++++ for 4 of 6 seeds. (31,15): +++-++-++++ or ++++-+-++++.
 (5) Implementability. c_c(x) differs between optima x in G by <= 8e-3. P Pi_c d is NOT a function of f: its within-level
 spread is 5e-4 to 1.4e-2. So the signs are computed here from x*. Whether they can be predicted from code-level data (the
 patterns repeat across seeds) is OPEN. The circuit uses a lookup phase on the score level: one coherent score evaluation
 plus a level-indexed phase, with the same score-register cost as a cost phase.
Restart-normalised, the K = 1 circuit is far from C_AD at these p, e.g. 3/0.0055 = 545 vs 57.8 at (63,18) s200.
CONCLUSION: W1c, the per-K form for score-function phases, is FALSE on dual-BCH DQI. Linear cost phases (R5.4) are a
special case that did not exhibit it.

## R6.2 Reference-subspace method for score phases (PROVED bound, numerically weak; negative for the method)
S_f = span{Pi_c d : c bad} is the smallest subspace containing b0 that is preserved by all score phases. It is preserved
by ancilla-controlled score operations and threshold-type operations (as S_f (x) A), and dist(d, S_f) = theta. The R5.3 argument
extends verbatim to the following.
Theorem Wf (PROVED). Let M = Pi_{S_f} P Pi_{S_f} (on S_f) and cos delta_W = min_{mu in spec M} |1 - 2mu|. Then any circuit
with K_D D-units, K_W wall-units and score/threshold-type free operations has success <= sin^2(theta + 2theta K_D + delta_W K_W)
(capped at 1). Also |1 - (1 - e^{ia}) mu|^2 = 1 - 4 mu(1-mu) sin^2(a/2), so the original W bound survives iff
mu(1-mu) <= p(1-p) for all mu. That criterion FAILS on all 24 instances (run48-51): delta_W/(2 theta) = 1.09-4.6, which allows a
restart lower bound as weak as 0.23 C_AD. Larger score-invariant subspaces S^(1), S^(2) (closures under P, levelwise)
make delta WORSE on the 6 (31,10) instances (ada/w1c_refsub.py, logs/run52; e.g. s202 2.07 -> 3.39 -> 3.92). The K1
violations show that no reference-subspace bound can reproduce B_1 here. The method cannot prove W1c, and W1c is false
per K anyway.

## R6.3 Does the gain compound? (NUMERICAL, best-found, bounded counterexample-driven test; w1c_multik.py, w1c_allw.py)
Arbitrary score-level phase vectors per unit, all D/W patterns for K <= 3 (run53), then all-wall K <= 8 warm-started (run56).
The K = 1 optimiser value equals the exact K1 value (0.10018), which validates the optimiser at K = 1.
 (31,10) s204 (p = 0.0111, C_AD = 13.06 at K = 5): best/B_K = 1.032 (K1), 1.055 (K2, WW), 1.038 (K3, WWW), 1.015 (K4)
 [run56 continues below]. All-wall circuits were best at every K. (63,12) s200: 1.023 (K1), 1.052 (K2, WW).
EOF
